I will keep this year simple and steady. I am in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so I will stay with the wheat and summer maize rotation that fits my land, weather, and the way I know how to farm. I want crops I can manage with familiar work, clear timing, and reliable buyers, not something risky that needs too much cash or technical skill. I will plant winter wheat first because it uses the winter-spring season well, then after harvest I will put the same land into summer maize. I will use improved seed because I want better yield and stronger disease resistance, but I will not choose an expensive, high-risk plan. I will use moderate fertilizer, not too much, because too much nitrogen can push weak growth and waste money. I will irrigate a few key times when the crop really needs it, especially for wheat at overwintering, jointing, and grain filling, and for maize after sowing and around tasseling. I will plough before wheat to set up the land well, then use rotary tillage before maize so I can turn the field around quickly after wheat harvest. I will spray only when needed, mainly for common weeds, aphids, rust, and corn borers, because I want to control losses without overspending. This is the plan I would follow because it is practical, familiar, and most likely to give me stable grain and income.
